name: caller-principal-node-session-stop-admits-an-absent-principal
description: KTD12 -- the Node side of fixture 03, with the identical setup and request: a claim for session A, then a session-stop naming A without a principal. Node answers the claim 404 and binds nothing (the harness asserts no preflight status below 500), and it enforces no principal, so it admits the stop that Python refuses because its claim bound A. The row pins exactly that answer, 200 {ok: true, released_artifacts: []}; A holds no grant here, so it shows the stop admitted, not a grant released. Unlike fixture 15 (a commit naming a session nobody claimed, admitted on both runtimes), the claim is what separates the two answers. Goes red the day Node answers this stop any other way: for example once Node both binds on the claim and refuses an absent principal for the session it bound, as Python does, or refuses every stop that carries no principal. Node adding only the claim route, while still enforcing nothing, leaves this row green -- fixture 01 is the row that goes red then.
